## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
## Observed
A coverage sweep of docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh (post-0.1.0) found two read/output-scoping flags on the concept-inspection commands are never exercised against the real binary, even though the bare commands and other flag combinations on the same commands are well covered:

- `lore validate --type <T>` — only bare `lore validate`, path-scoped `lore validate <paths...>`, and `--strict` appear in the harness. The type-filter path (skip files whose type doesn't match) is untested.
- `lore schema export --type <T>` and `lore schema export --out <dir>` — only bare `lore schema export --json` appears (multiple times, always exporting every type to the default `.lore/schemas/` location). Single-type export and a custom output directory are untested.

## Why it matters
Both flags are part of the documented, `--help`-exposed contract (`lore help validate --json`, `lore help schema --json`) and are exactly the kind of real-filesystem/real-argument-parsing behavior this project's own precedent (LCLI-56, LCLI-66) treats as needing the real-binary gate rather than relying on unit tests alone.

## Direction (decide in plan)
Add small E2E assertions near the existing validate/schema-export phases: `lore validate --type <T>` on a mixed-type bundle only reports on files of that type; `lore schema export --type <T>` writes only that type's schema file; `lore schema export --out <dir>` writes into the custom directory instead of `.lore/schemas/`. Re-derive exact flag names/behavior from `lore help validate --json` / `lore help schema --json` and src/commands/validate.ts / src/commands/schema.ts at execution time rather than trusting this description.
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->

## Acceptance Criteria
<!-- AC:BEGIN -->
- [x] #1 lore validate --type <T> on a mixed-type bundle reports only on files of that type, asserted E2E
- [x] #2 lore schema export --type <T> writes only that type's schema file, asserted E2E
- [x] #3 lore schema export --out <dir> writes schemas into the custom directory instead of the default .lore/schemas/, asserted E2E
- [x] #4 The full harness runs green against the real pinned binary, and teardown is clean
<!-- AC:END -->

## Implementation Plan

<!-- SECTION:PLAN:BEGIN -->
1. In Phase 8, run `lore validate --type ADR --json` against the already mixed six-type bundle and assert the known ADR path is included, the known Reference path is excluded, every returned file is canonical type ADR, and the report is clean.
2. In Phase 17, export `--type Story` into a fresh probe directory; assert the structured result names exactly one Story schema and the directory contains only that valid JSON file.
3. Export the full active profile with `--out` into a second fresh directory; assert the result reports all six files under that directory, none under `.lore/schemas`, and every expected schema is valid JSON.
4. Remove only the exact probe-created schema files and directories, assert teardown, then run shell parsing, diff hygiene, the complete Docker E2E harness, proportionate repository gates, and adversarial self-review.
<!-- SECTION:PLAN:END -->

## Implementation Notes

<!-- SECTION:NOTES:BEGIN -->
Research re-derived the contract from the current help manifest, `src/commands/validate.ts`, `src/core/validate.ts`, `src/commands/schema.ts`, unit tests, and the live harness. `validate --type` preserves broken files intentionally but a clean mixed bundle can assert exact ADR scoping. `schema export` reports `{out, files, removed, count}`; isolated relative output directories make both scoping behaviors directly observable without disturbing the managed default schema set.

Implemented the planned Phase 8 and Phase 17 probes in docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh. `bash -n` and `git diff --check` pass. The live local `validate --type ADR --json` report satisfied the core scoping predicate, and synthetic structured payloads proved both new schema-result jq filters parse and evaluate true before the full container run.

Objective verification: full rebuilt Docker E2E passed 329/329 with 0 failures. The persisted report has exactly 329 PASS records; its LCLI-299 entries show the mixed bundle returned only the known ADR, single-type export reported and wrote exactly one valid Story schema, custom output reported and wrote all six valid schemas outside `.lore/schemas`, and both probe directories were absent after teardown.

Repository gates: `bun test` passed 2,434 tests with 0 failures; `bun run typecheck` passed; `bun run lint` checked 186 files with no fixes; `bash -n docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh` and `git diff --check` passed. Docker Compose shows the E2E container Exited (0).

Adversarial self-review: the validate assertion is non-vacuous because it pins both a known included ADR path and a known excluded Reference path. Both schema probes require initially absent directories, assert exact structured path sets and independent valid-JSON filesystem results, delete only named files, require `rmdir` success, and assert both directories absent. Unexpected extra output therefore makes teardown or the final assertion fail. No independent reviewer was authorized; no residual risk or scope expansion was found.

Local delivery completed in source commit 106219c. The commit contains only docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh with 61 insertions. No fetch, push, PR, merge, publication, or remote mutation occurred.
<!-- SECTION:NOTES:END -->

## Final Summary

<!-- SECTION:FINAL_SUMMARY:BEGIN -->
Delivered persistent real-binary coverage for `lore validate --type`, `lore schema export --type`, and `lore schema export --out` in local source commit 106219c. The new assertions prove non-vacuous type filtering on a mixed bundle, exact single-schema output, full custom-directory output outside the managed default path, valid JSON artifacts, and exact teardown. Verification passed Docker E2E 329/329, 2,434 unit/integration tests, typecheck, lint, shell parsing, diff hygiene, and adversarial self-review.
<!-- SECTION:FINAL_SUMMARY:END -->
